🎙️ 👔 Luciano Spalletti: “The disallowed goal? Well, the referee is a good official, although perhaps a little less good when it came to making the decision in that particular incident. “I don’t know the rules perfectly, but the way the incident unfolded certainly leaves room for interpretation. I was very disappointed when I watched it again in the locker room. “Lucumi made a mistake with his movement, but it wasn’t as though anyone had interfered with him. Considering that we should always encourage attacking football and the pursuit of goals, I felt the goal should have stood.” “Çelik felt some muscle tightness, but he’s a very alert player and recognised the problem. However, recovering him in just two days will be difficult.”

‼️ JUVENTUS HOLD CRISIS MEETING AT CONTINASSA — FULL BACKING FOR SPALLETTI! 👥 Juventus management, Luciano Spalletti and the first-team squad reportedly held a crucial meeting at Continassa to address the team’s recent struggles. 😑 The players accepted responsibility for their poor performances, acknowledging lapses in concentration, intensity and determination. 🤝 Juventus directors reaffirmed their full confidence in Spalletti, making it clear that his position is not under discussion. 🙌🏻 The squad also expressed support for the coach’s tactical approach and commitment to turning results around. The message from Continassa: Juventus remain united and determined to overcome the crisis together. ⚪️ ⚫️

‼️ 🇧🇷 BREMER APOLOGISES TO SPALLETTI AND TEAMMATES — JUVENTUS WILL FINE THE DEFENDER Gleison Bremer has apologised to Luciano Spalletti and his teammates following his post-match comments after the 3–0 defeat against Lazio. The Brazilian admitted that frustration and anger had influenced his remarks to Sky Sport. Spalletti has demanded greater individual accountability, insisting that players must assess their own performances before criticising others. Bremer, currently captaining Juventus in Manuel Locatelli’s absence, is reportedly set to receive a fine from the club, which he has already accepted. Juventus are now demanding a united response, with greater discipline and responsibility throughout the squad. ⚪️ ⚫️

‼️ DI GREGORIO COULD LEAVE BOURNEMOUTH AFTER JUST SIX MONTHS — BOLOGNA INTERESTED Juventus goalkeeper Michele Di Gregorio could cut short his loan spell at Bournemouth in January. The Italian has reportedly fallen to second choice and could push for an early exit to secure a return to Serie A. Bologna are monitoring his situation, with Raffaele Palladino — who previously coached Di Gregorio at Monza — a big admirer of the goalkeeper.
